privacy_why_anon_body: Reports are linked to a private device ID that we cannot trace back to you. No phone number, no email, no login needed. You can use the app forever without revealing who you are.
privacy_why_offline_body: The app works in low-connectivity zones. Reports queue locally on your device and upload automatically once the network is back. You never lose what you've captured.
privacy_why_blur_body: Faces are detected and blurred on your phone before the photo is uploaded. The server never sees an unredacted face. This is a UNDP requirement (§2.9) and a CRISP guarantee.
privacy_collect_1: Photos you take (with faces blurred client-side)
privacy_collect_4: GPS coordinates at the time of capture
privacy_collect_5: Crisis type, infrastructure type, and damage classification you select
privacy_collect_6: A SHA-256 hash of your device fingerprint (your reporter ID)
privacy_never_3: Your phone number or email (unless you choose to sign in)
privacy_never_4: Browser fingerprints, tracking pixels, or advertising IDs
privacy_never_5: Your contacts, photos library, or any data outside what you explicitly submit
privacy_rights_1: Delete any single report (per-report Delete button on the detail view)
privacy_rights_2: Delete all your reports at once (Settings → Delete all my reports)
privacy_rights_3: 24-hour soft-delete grace — you can undo deletion within 24 hours before permanent removal
privacy_rights_4: Export your reports as JSON / CSV (Settings → Export my data — coming soon)
privacy_rights_5: Anonymous reports stay anonymous forever; we cannot unblind them
privacy_opensrc_body: CRISP is open source under the Apache-2.0 licence. The code is published on GitHub. You can audit how your data is handled, propose changes, or self-host the platform.
privacy_how_1_b: Take a photo, record a voice note, or type a quick description. Any one is enough — all three is even better.
privacy_how_2_b: Tap to tell us how bad the damage is, what was hit, and what caused it. Plain-language tiles — no jargon.
privacy_how_3_b: Tap Send. If you're offline, the report queues and uploads automatically when the network is back.
privacy_channels_body: You can report through the PWA (this app), the Android app, an SMS, an IVR call (voice phone tree), a WhatsApp message, or a Telegram chat. Every channel produces the same report on the responder side, with the same protections.
